A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 26-page versions of the same research work. Their corresponding sections, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–D support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix C report original experiments on representation learning, imputation and conditional generation, including measured reconstruction errors, likelihoods and training times.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and their numerical and qualitative outcomes, including the main results and appendix sensitivity studies.

M1.justification: GPVAE-HPA and GPVAE-SPA retain the same prior approximations, encoder architecture, training objectives, mini-batch inference and predictive procedures in Section 3 and Appendix B.

E1.justification: Both evaluate moving-ball representation learning, corrupted- and missing-frame Rotated MNIST, MuJoCo conditional generation, and Jura/SPE10 imputation. Section 5 and Appendix C contain no added or removed dataset or test scenario.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within the corresponding main-text and appendix experiments. The new Tran et al. (2021a) citation in Appendix D supports background discussion; it does not introduce an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: The data splits, masking rates, kernels, neighbour and inducing-point counts, model configurations, training budgets and evaluation procedures remain unchanged in Section 5 and Appendix C.

E4.justification: The neighbour-count sensitivity analyses in Figure 2b and Tables 6, 9 and 11 are retained unchanged. Appendix C also retains the same qualitative reconstruction, generation and imputation examples.

E5.justification: Both specify means and standard deviations from 10 random trials. Figure 2's uncertainty bands, the 95% predictive intervals in Figures 4 and 11, and Appendix C's seed-related disclosures are unchanged.

E6.justification: The numerical results and qualitative displays match throughout, including Appendix C. For example, Table 2 retains GPVAE-HPA-H10's MuJoCo NLL of -2.335 ± 0.032 and RMSE of 0.0222 ± 0.001.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations and derivations in Section 3 and Appendices B and D are unchanged. Appendix D.1 replaces '=' with ':=' when naming latent pseudo-observations and noise; this is equivalent definitional notation, not revised mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims concerning two neighbour-driven GPVAE approximations, flexible kernels, scalable inference, and predictive accuracy and computational efficiency.

C2.justification: The explanations of experimental performance and the limitations concerning Euclidean distance and alternative neighbourhood metrics remain unchanged. The shortened Impact Statement introduces no substantive qualification, and SGPBAE's Bayesian-autoencoder classification already appeared in v1.

D1.justification: Appendix C retains the same implementation repository, software, hardware, architectures and hyperparameter information. Removed bibliography URLs concern cited publications, not access to the work's code or data.

R1.justification: v3 adds Tran et al., Model selection for Bayesian autoencoders (2021a), to support Appendix D's existing description of SGPBAE. The previously cited nearest-neighbour GP paper becomes Tran et al. (2021b). This is a limited attribution addition without substantive repositioning.

P1.justification: Limited copyediting corrects 'GPAVEs/GPAVE' and 'regerssion', changes 'inducing point distribution' to 'inducing variable distribution', streamlines the Impact Statement, and tidies bibliography capitalization and metadata. The section and appendix structure remains intact.

P2.justification: v3 colors citations, internal cross-references and the repository link, with minor text and bibliography reflow. All 11 figures and 15 tables retain their content and organization; the plotted imagery and graphical results are unchanged.

improvement.justification: Corrected technical wording and typos, the added Bayesian-autoencoder attribution in Appendix D, and visibly distinguished cross-references provide a small clarity and usability improvement. Methods, evidence and reproducibility remain unchanged. Removing several bibliography URLs slightly reduces direct-source convenience, limiting the net gain to modest editorial refinement.
